name: stacking-card
title: Stacking Card
description: A photographer's project list where each large coloured card sticks near the top of the screen and the next slides up over it. Each card pairs a short bio and See more link with a big image panel.
use: A creative portfolio wants each project to get its own full screen without separate pages.
avoid: Each card takes a full screen, so five projects cost five screens of scrolling, and every link goes to #.
a11y: The artwork alt text is just image, the smooth scroll takes over the native feel, and reduced-motion is not honoured. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Wide rounded cards in periwinkle, lavender and deep indigo on a near-black page, each with a centred white name, a small bio and underlined See more on the left, and a large blue-and-white mosaic panel on the right. A dark hero with a faint grid opens the page.
behaves: Scrolling holds each card near the top while the following card rises from below to cover it, so the stack builds downward. The covered card shrinks slightly and its inner panel zooms back out before the group scrolls away.
customise: The page takes no props: the five projects, names, bios, links and card colours are set in the projects array in the file.
weight: moderate: Five remote images and per-frame scroll transforms stretched over five screens.
demo: Photographers named Matthias Leidinger, Clément Chapillon and Zissou, with short bios.
issues: Every See more link points to #, so no project can be opened.
The image panels show abstract blue shapes rather than the photography the bios describe.
White card names sit on pale periwinkle and lavender with weak contrast.
The caption text is very small against the width of each card.
polishWhy: Strong colour blocking and a smooth stack; tiny text, weak contrast and placeholder links.
